help-getting-started.title: getting-started
help-getting-started.summary: Start with an intention, add a route, and link its steps to architectural components and explanations. hmap render shows every line; --route selects a slice.
help-getting-started.explanation: Start with an intention, add a route, and link its steps to architectural components and explanations. hmap render shows every line; --route selects a slice.

help-commands.title: commands
help-commands.summary: Commands: help, template, schema, validate, import, normalize, render, inspect, hints, explain, export, migrate. Input may be a file or - for stdin.
help-commands.explanation: Commands: help, template, schema, validate, import, normalize, render, inspect, hints, explain, export, migrate. Input may be a file or - for stdin.

help-json.title: json
help-json.summary: Canonical data is strict UTF-8 JSON schema 2. IDs are global; unknown fields and duplicate keys are errors.
help-json.explanation: Canonical data is strict UTF-8 JSON schema 2. IDs are global; unknown fields and duplicate keys are errors.

help-roadmap-text.title: roadmap-text
help-roadmap-text.summary: RoadmapText/1 uses keyword id {JSON fields} records and <<route:id>> [step] -> [step] <<end-route>> blocks. Each step belongs to one block. Use hmap template --format=roadmap-text for all required fields.
help-roadmap-text.explanation: RoadmapText/1 uses keyword id {JSON fields} records and <<route:id>> [step] -> [step] <<end-route>> blocks. Each step belongs to one block. Use hmap template --format=roadmap-text for all required fields.

help-llm.title: llm
help-llm.summary: Return a complete RoadmapText/1 document, preserve existing IDs, declare every reference and use unknown with a reason. No outer Markdown fence. Run hmap validate candidate.roadmap.txt --format=json. Obtain the complete grammar with help roadmap-text, field definitions with schema, and a self-contained example with template --format=roadmap-text.

help-intents.title: intents
help-intents.summary: An intention states an observable desired result. Its parents describe origin; acceptanceCriteria describe acceptance. Every intention immediately begins its own map line.
help-intents.explanation: An intention states an observable desired result. Its parents describe origin; acceptanceCriteria describe acceptance. Every intention immediately begins its own map line.

help-routes.title: routes
help-routes.summary: A route is an ordered scenario for one intention. Add a step after selecting a route. Several intentions and routes appear together. Selection sets the editing context and establishes no scheduling dependency.
help-routes.explanation: A route is an ordered scenario for one intention. Add a step after selecting a route. Several intentions and routes appear together. Selection sets the editing context and establishes no scheduling dependency.

help-reuse.title: reuse
help-reuse.summary: Reuse is established by multiple steps referencing the same module ID. Each occurrence keeps its own step ID.
help-reuse.explanation: Reuse is established by multiple steps referencing the same module ID. Each occurrence keeps its own step ID.

help-estimates.title: estimates
help-estimates.summary: range effort means person-minutes; elapsed means calendar minutes. Unknown ?, not-applicable n/a, text and missing - are distinct. Totals are outside schema 2.
help-estimates.explanation: range effort means person-minutes; elapsed means calendar minutes. Unknown ?, not-applicable n/a, text and missing - are distinct. Totals are outside schema 2.

help-continuous-intents.title: continuous-intents
help-continuous-intents.summary: A continuous intention stays active while maintained or deferred while suspended. Describe initial implementation and recurring review separately.
help-continuous-intents.explanation: A continuous intention stays active while maintained or deferred while suspended. Describe initial implementation and recurring review separately.

help-references.title: references
help-references.summary: IDs use [a-z][a-z0-9]*(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*, 1..64 ASCII bytes. Update references in one complete candidate. Intersections accept intentions, modules, chunks and steps.
help-references.explanation: IDs use [a-z][a-z0-9]*(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*, 1..64 ASCII bytes. Update references in one complete candidate. Intersections accept intentions, modules, chunks and steps.

help-storage.title: storage
help-storage.summary: Save explicitly. LocalStorage belongs to one origin and one active writer; download JSON as a backup. A temporary session is held only in memory.
help-storage.explanation: Save explicitly. LocalStorage belongs to one origin and one active writer; download JSON as a backup. A temporary session is held only in memory.

help-export.title: export
help-export.summary: JSON is the accepted source. RoadmapText is reversible transport. Markdown is a deterministic projection; --route creates a labelled slice.
help-export.explanation: JSON is the accepted source. RoadmapText is reversible transport. Markdown is a deterministic projection; --route creates a labelled slice.

help-wasm.title: wasm
help-wasm.summary: The same C++ engine runs in one Worker. Await readiness, serve JS/Wasm from one build, and dispose owned workers. No project data is sent to a server.
help-wasm.explanation: The same C++ engine runs in one Worker. Await readiness, serve JS/Wasm from one build, and dispose owned workers. No project data is sent to a server.

hint-acceptance.title: acceptance
hint-acceptance.summary: What observable result will establish acceptance?
hint-acceptance.explanation: What observable result will establish acceptance?

hint-acceptance-evidence.title: acceptance-evidence
hint-acceptance-evidence.summary: Where is the explanation of acceptance recorded?
hint-acceptance-evidence.explanation: Where is the explanation of acceptance recorded?

hint-reuse.title: reuse
hint-reuse.summary: Does the module contract remain valid in every occurrence?
hint-reuse.explanation: Does the module contract remain valid in every occurrence?

hint-unknown.title: unknown
hint-unknown.summary: What must be learned to refine this estimate?
hint-unknown.explanation: What must be learned to refine this estimate?

hint-days.title: days
hint-days.summary: Does this mean calendar duration or working effort?
hint-days.explanation: Does this mean calendar duration or working effort?

hint-continuous.title: continuous
hint-continuous.summary: Where are initial implementation, recurring review and maintenance described?
hint-continuous.explanation: Where are initial implementation, recurring review and maintenance described?

hint-code.title: code
hint-code.summary: Which code or artifact represents this existing module?
hint-code.explanation: Which code or artifact represents this existing module?

hint-chunk.title: chunk
hint-chunk.summary: What role does this unlinked fragment have in the project?
hint-chunk.explanation: What role does this unlinked fragment have in the project?

help-intersections.title: intersections
help-intersections.summary: An intersection records a named relationship between at least two different intentions, steps, components or explanations. Select two sources in its form. Routes and estimates are excluded. For example, connect two steps that rely on the same contract; reference a shared component from both steps to express actual reuse.
help-intersections.explanation: An intersection records a named relationship between at least two different intentions, steps, components or explanations. Select two sources in its form. Routes and estimates are excluded. For example, connect two steps that rely on the same contract; reference a shared component from both steps to express actual reuse.

help-workflow.title: workflow
help-workflow.summary: Begin with an intention. Components, explanations, estimates and routes then become available. A step requires a selected route. An intersection requires two eligible sources, and its form requires two selected sources. hmap render displays all intention-led lines, including intentions without routes; hmap render map.roadmap.json --route=r-main selects one route. Existing imported unlinked components remain valid.
help-workflow.explanation: Begin with an intention. Components, explanations, estimates and routes then become available. A step requires a selected route. An intersection requires two eligible sources, and its form requires two selected sources. hmap render displays all intention-led lines, including intentions without routes; hmap render map.roadmap.json --route=r-main selects one route. Existing imported unlinked components remain valid.

codes.E_INPUT_LIMIT: A declared resource limit was exceeded. Reduce input or review the limit manifest.
codes.E_PARSE_JSON: Correct JSON syntax at the reported byte location.
codes.E_PARSE_TEXT: Correct the RoadmapText record or route grammar.
codes.E_DUPLICATE_KEY: Each object key must occur once.
codes.E_SCHEMA_VERSION: Use schema 2 or explicitly migrate schema 1.
codes.E_FIELD_UNKNOWN: Use only fields declared for this record.
codes.E_FIELD_TYPE: Supply the required field with its declared type and allowed value.
codes.E_ID_INVALID: Use a stable lowercase ASCII ID, 1..64 bytes.
codes.E_ID_DUPLICATE: Each entity needs a globally unique ID.
codes.E_REF_NOT_FOUND: Declare the missing target or correct the reference.
codes.E_REF_TYPE: Reference an entity of the required type.
codes.E_REF_DUPLICATE: Keep one occurrence of each reference in this array.
codes.E_ROUTE_MEMBERSHIP: Declare one block per route and place each step in exactly one block.
codes.E_SELECTION: Select a route belonging to the selected intention.
codes.E_INTENT_CYCLE: Remove the reported cycle in intention lineage.
codes.E_INTENT_CONTINUOUS_STATUS: A continuous intention remains active or deferred.
codes.E_ESTIMATE_RANGE: Use integer minutes 0..1000000000 with minimum <= maximum.
codes.E_ESTIMATE_REASON: Explain why the estimate is unknown or not applicable.
codes.W_ROUTE_EMPTY: The empty route remains a valid draft.
codes.W_ESTIMATE_BASIS_MISSING: Describe the observation or assumption behind the estimate.
codes.W_UNREFERENCED_OBJECT: Review the unused object; it is preserved.
codes.E_COMMAND: Review the command and supported options.
codes.E_IO_READ: The input file could not be read.
codes.E_IO_WRITE: The output could not be installed; inspect permissions and free space.
codes.E_OUTPUT_EXISTS: Choose another output or explicitly use --overwrite.
codes.E_STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE: Storage access is unavailable. Download JSON to preserve the project.
codes.E_STORAGE_QUOTA: Storage quota is exhausted. Download JSON.
codes.E_STORAGE_CORRUPT: Stored data is invalid and has been preserved for recovery.
codes.E_STORAGE_CONFLICT: Another writer changed this project. Reload or save a copy.
codes.E_INTERNAL: An unexpected engine error occurred; the last accepted project is retained.
codes.W_MIGRATION_DEFAULT: Review all migration defaults before accepting this candidate.

host.The map was restored with unsaved change: The map was restored with unsaved changes.
host.The architecture example is open. Edit i: The architecture example is open. Edit it or create a new map.
host.This version was saved. The current map: This version was saved. The current map has newer unsaved changes.
host.The map is saved for this session. Downl: The map is saved for this session. Download JSON to transfer it.
The map is saved in this browser.
The saved map was not found.
host.The map passed validation with no errors: The map passed validation with no errors or warnings.
host.The map connects a desired result to the: The map connects a desired result to the architecture and the route that will realise it. Each intention immediately begins a line; several intentions and alternative routes can be developed together.
host.Create an intention: describe the result: Create an intention: describe the result and its observable criteria. It appears in the horizontal map immediately.
host.Select its line and add a route. A route: Select its line and add a route. A route describes one way to realise that intention.
host.Add architectural components and contrac: Add architectural components and contracts or explanations. These are reusable records with stable identities.
host.Add steps to the selected route. In each: Add steps to the selected route. In each step, choose the existing components and explanations it uses. A step describes an action; a component describes part of the system.
host.Select a step to reveal its linked recor: Select a step to reveal its linked records above. Use Edit to change it and Validate map to check the document.
host.Apply a form, then save the map explicit: Apply a form, then save the map explicitly. File → Download JSON transfers the accepted map to another browser through Import.
host.Intention is always available. Other cre: Intention is always available. Other creation actions open after the first intention. Existing imported records remain available for editing.
host.Route requires a selected intention. Rou: Route requires a selected intention. Route step requires a selected route; use its line to choose the destination.
host.Intersection requires at least two exist: Intersection requires at least two existing intentions, steps, components or explanations. Its form stays inactive until two different sources are selected. Routes and estimates are excluded.
host.An intersection names a relationship wor: An intersection names a relationship worth explaining: for example, two steps depend on the same validation contract. Write the relationship in its note and choose its sources. Actual component reuse is expressed by both steps referencing the same component.
host.Add another intention to start another l: Add another intention to start another line. Add another route to explore an alternative for the same intention. Components and explanations can be shared across lines by identity; their names remain free to change. The arrows describe a route, while scheduling and time totals need a separate model.
host.Schema 2 is shared by CLI and WebAssembl: Schema 2 is shared by CLI and WebAssembly. Language changes interface labels and help; authored text and machine IDs keep their original values. Maps are saved in this browser. JSON transfers the full map; Markdown provides a readable export.
